s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of sharp precordial pain with persistent symptoms and abnormal cardiac sounds
salient_findings: Sporadic clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
Normal lung and heart auscultation except for intermittent clicking
key_facts: 19-year-old man with no past medical history
Three-week history of persistent sharp precordial pain
Pain began during an episode of gastroenteritis
Gastrointestinal symptoms resolved while chest pain remained
Pain worsened on inspiration
Clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge
Normal vital signs
Normal lung and heart auscultation except for clicking
Normal laboratory studies, including arterial blood gas, complete blood count, and cardiac troponins
Normal chest radiograph
Normal electrocardiography

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Persistent sharp precordial pain and abnormal cardiac sounds

shortlist.label: Mitral valve prolapse
shortlist.why_kept: Clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge

shortlist.label: Costochondritis
shortlist.why_kept: Pain worsened on inspiration and normal laboratory studies

shortlist.label: Precordial catch syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp precordial pain and normal electrocardiography

shortlist.label: Tietze syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Pain and clicking sound on the left sternal edge with normal vital signs

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of sharp precordial pain that worsens on inspiration, along with a clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge, are consistent with precordial catch syndrome, which is a benign condition characterized by recurrent, sharp chest pain and is often associated with a clicking or popping sound.

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Normal laboratory studies, including cardiac troponins, and normal electrocardiography make pericarditis less likely

rejected.label: Mitral valve prolapse
rejected.why: Normal heart auscultation and lack of other symptoms such as shortness of breath or palpitations make mitral valve prolapse less likely

rejected.label: Costochondritis
rejected.why: The presence of a clicking and popping sound on the left sternal edge is not typical of costochondritis, which usually presents with tenderness to palpation of the costochondral junctions

rejected.label: Tietze syndrome
rejected.why: Tietze syndrome typically presents with swelling and tenderness of the costochondral junctions, which is not mentioned in the patient's presentation
